chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: 'Amr ibn Abi Nasr narrated to me, saying:
I said to Abu 'Abd Allah (AS): 'I urinate, perform wudu, and forget my istinja', then I remember after having prayed.'
He (AS) said: 'Wash your private part, repeat your prayer, and do not repeat your wudu.'

key_terms.اِسْتِنْجَاء: istinja' — ritual cleansing of the private parts after relieving oneself, a prerequisite for salat
key_terms.ذَكَر: the male private part — the organ requiring washing before the prayer is valid
key_terms.صَلاَة: salat — obligatory ritual prayer, which must be repeated when performed without istinja'
key_terms.وُضُوء: wudu — ritual ablution; ruled here to remain valid despite the forgotten istinja'

ai.seo_question: If a person forgets istinja' after urinating, performs wudu, and prays — must they repeat both the wudu and the prayer, or only the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling (hukm shar'i) from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) on a case where a man urinates, performs wudu, forgets istinja' (cleansing the private part after urination), and only remembers after completing his salat. The Imam ruled that he must wash the private part and repeat the salat, but his wudu remains valid and need not be repeated — establishing that istinja' is a precondition for the validity of salat, not for wudu.
